data.one_liner: FFI-based implementation of sqflite for desktop platforms and unit tests.
data.what_it_does: Provides an sqflite-compatible database interface using the sqlite3 FFI package. Enables running SQLite databases on Windows, macOS, Linux, and during standard Flutter unit tests without device emulators.
use_when: You need sqflite-based SQLite database support on Windows, macOS, or Linux.
You want to write and execute unit tests involving sqflite without a physical device or emulator.
avoid_when: You are building exclusively for mobile platforms where standard sqflite or drift is preferred.
You require advanced reactive query streams out-of-the-box without extra boilerplate.
strengths: Brings familiar sqflite API to desktop platforms and unit tests.
Database calls are executed in a separate isolate.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific setup on Linux (libsqlite3 packages).
Database calls in a separate isolate and multi-instance support is simulated.
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing with sqfliteFfiInit(). On Linux, requires installing libsqlite3 packages (e.g. libsqlite3-0 and libsqlite3-dev).

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a type-safe reactive SQL database library with code generation for Dart and Flutter.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need standard SQLite access on iOS and Android.

alternatives.name: hive_ce
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a fast key-value NoSQL database instead of a relational SQL database.
